agree.reason: The draft answers the late shelving report head-on, names a responsible person and promises quarterly totals, so Marisol has reason to recommend it, though the unfunded $4,500 a year may still give her pause.

honest.reason: The doubling claim is correctly dropped, but 'it went to waste', 'no one else was assigned' and 'the single biggest thing holding back' are claims the brief doesn't support.

works_the_facts.reason: It correctly works out 3,000 lb a month as a 50% rise in fresh food during harvest months and puts the figure in that favourable form, but it never states the yearly effect or shows that the $11,000 left in reserve could carry the running costs.

right_comparison.reason: The status quo is described as continuing to turn food away, which is accurate, but saying the food 'went to waste' goes beyond what the facts show about what happened to it.

qualification.reason: It admits the farm offers may not repeat and commits to quarterly totals and a final report due 30 days after the grant year ends, but it sets no target, gives no quarterly dates and says nothing about what happens if fresh pounds fall short.

objections.reason: The reporting objection is met well, but the draft raises the unbudgeted $4,500 a year and then leaves it without any plan for paying it.

fit.reason: This is a well-sectioned grant narrative of about 475 words, within the 500-word limit.
